turns.query: Our pH probe has been in the water two seasons and the readings feel sluggish. After I run a fresh calibration, what number should I be looking at to tell me the electrode itself is still any good, and what counts as passing?

relevant.evidence:
The slope test—Properly working electrodes should
have slopes that are 56.2 to 59.8 mV/pH unit at
25 °C, which is 95 to 101 percent of the expected
slope from the theoretical Nernst relation
relevant.locator: Section 4.1.1 steps 10j-12, the slope test — "Properly working electrodes should have slopes that are 56.2 to 59.8 mV/pH unit at 25 °C"

relevant.evidence:
The ideal slope of the calibration curve
at 25 °C, based on the Nernst equation (see section 2.2), is
59.16 mV/pH unit.
relevant.locator: Section 3.3 long-term storage and section 4.0 Calibration of the pH Instrument System — "A calibration curve is created by measurement of two or more standard pH buffers"

relevant.evidence:
a pH electrode with an accurate Nernstian response
(slope of 95–101 percent of the theoretical
Nernstian slope)
relevant.locator: Section 4.0 Calibration of the pH Instrument System — "A properly working pH system has—"

relevant.evidence:
Reconditioning
procedures should be implemented if the electrode’s slope
response has deteriorated to less than 95 percent or greater
than 101 percent
relevant.locator: Section 3.2 Reconditioning (Flushing and Refilling) of Liquid-Filled Electrodes — "If problems persist during calibration"

relevant.evidence:
If the slope
falls outside this range, do not use the electrode.
relevant.locator: Section 3.2 reconditioning steps 3-4 and section 3.3 Electrode Storage — "Flush and fill the electrode with fresh filling solution"

relevant.evidence:
Clean, recondition, or replace the electrode if, after reca-
libration, the slope remains outside the acceptable range
of 95 to 101 percent
relevant.locator: Section 4.1.1 step 12 slope and millivolt tests, technical note, and section 4.1.2 — "The millivolt test"

relevant.evidence: Replace calibration buffers that yield inaccurate results with fresh NIST-traceable buffers.
relevant.locator: Table 6.4-4 Troubleshooting guide for pH measurement — "Symptom / Possible cause—corrective action"
